examples.why: Invoked members are printed as an opaque token helper even though the field-access path already resolves names (v0.Queue, v1.Yaw). 952 call sites lose the member name; the reader sees ResourcesPaid/GiveResources nowhere.
examples.fix: Resolve the member name at the call token and print receiver.Member(args). Keep the token only for the deliberate call-vs-callvirt precision cases and for generic method instantiations that still need their instantiation rendered.
examples.risk: low; presentation only. The exception is __cil_direct_ (199 sites) which encodes 'call not callvirt' on virtual this-accessors - keep that precision, add the name next to it.

examples.why: Lifter slot locals (e<slot>_<depth>_<n> and s<slot>_<depth>) leak into the output as if they were source variables. 821 of them across the slice; s9_0 is the ternary merge slot and e5_9_0/e7_9_0/e8_9_0 are its arms.
examples.fix: Rename slot temporaries to a scheme that cannot collide with source locals, then fold single-use merge slots back into ?: / ?? once each arm is proven side-effect free.
examples.risk: none for the rename; medium for the fold (needs a purity + single-use proof on the slot).

examples.why: __name_4F70656E... decodes to OpenRA.Traits.INotifyAddedToWorld.AddedToWorld; every explicit interface implementation gets a hex name (52 in the slice) plus 'private', and the delegated call loses its member name.
examples.fix: Print the interface-qualified member name for explicit implementations and drop the synthetic 'private'; for generated types print the demangled form (<>c__DisplayClass49_0 -> DisplayClass49_0) instead of the hex.
examples.risk: none - naming only. Inlining the closures themselves is the separate deliberate gap.

examples.why: Auto-property backing fields are emitted as fields named after their metadata token (421 in the slice) and the property itself becomes get_/set_ methods, so the type's API surface is invisible.
examples.fix: Detect the auto-property pair (backing field + get_/set_ accessors with matching visibility) and print one property declaration; use { get; set; } instead of the __il_field_* field.
examples.risk: low - same accessors and accessibility, only the member shape changes.

examples.why: The false branch is a goto to the label that is already the next line, so the else block is dead text; the condition is also inverted. 406 such pairs in the slice (Aircraft 181, Mobile 118, ProductionQueue 100, LobbyCommands 7).
examples.fix: Drop an else/goto pair whose target is the immediately following label; drop IL_xxxx: ; labels that no remaining goto references; negate the condition instead of branching around a single statement when the CFG already guarantees a two-way split.
examples.risk: none for the two deletions (they remove text the CFG already implies); low for the negation, which reorders the same two edges and should be checked by the existing structural validation.

examples.why: Locals are declared at the top and initialized to default, then reassigned before first read (475 sites); unchecked is nested twice on the same conversion (462 sites); the float math is printed as raw CLI ops (__cil_conv_r4, __cil_ldc_r4_bits(0x437F0000u), __cil_div_F, __cil_call_arg_r4) instead of (float)x / 255f.
examples.fix: Suppress '= default' when a definite-assignment pass shows the local is written before every read, drop the final 'return;' in void bodies, fold 'v = expr; return v;' for single-use temps, collapse nested unchecked((T)(unchecked((U)x))) to one conversion, and print float math from the ldc.r4 constant value.
examples.risk: none for the first three; low for the unchecked collapse; removing unchecked entirely would change behavior under /checked+ so that stays a separate decision.

examples.why: Every bool is loaded to an int and compared against 0 (290 __cil_bool_load + 132 __cil_bool_store), and the negated comparison is printed as !(x == 0) rather than x != 0.
examples.fix: Keep the bool type through the lift (print bool locals and conditions as bool), print != instead of !(x == 0), and fold 'if (c) return X; if (d) return X;' where the two returns are identical.
examples.risk: low - same predicates and same returns.

examples.why: Returning default(T) goes through a ref alias to the hoisted local, producing three statements and a live ref local where the source had 'return null'.
examples.fix: When the returned value is the default of a nullable/value type and the local has no other reader, return the literal (null for Nullable<T>) directly and drop the ref alias.
examples.risk: low - requires only a single-use check on the local.

examples.why: Every character of every const string is escaped: 37 literals, 1321 \uXXXX escapes. The same printer renders ordinary literals readably elsewhere (__cil_ldstr_70000931("state")), so the defect is confined to the const-initializer path.
examples.fix: Escape only \" , backslash and control characters; print everything else literally (line 4841's \u000A must stay escaped).
examples.risk: none - round-trip is preserved because non-printable characters still escape.

examples.why: Types are spelled three ways at once: fully qualified with global:: (1026 sites), with @ escapes on OpenRA's own namespace segments (188 sites), and as a structural alias (2938 sites). ILSpy uses short names through a using block (0 using directives on our side, 35 on ILSpy's).
examples.fix: Emit a using block for resolved namespaces and print short names; strip @ on non-keyword identifiers; map __cil_* aliases to the resolved type name; keep global:: only for names that genuinely conflict.
examples.risk: low, with one caveat: global::/@ were presumably added to guarantee unambiguity, so gate the short-name path on 'no shadowing in scope' instead of deleting the escape unconditionally.

examples.why: Operator overloads are printed by their metadata name (75 sites: op_Inequality, op_Equality) instead of the operator token, and the expression-bodied property is expanded into a body.
examples.fix: Map op_Equality/op_Inequality/op_Addition/... to the operator token; collapse to an expression body when the body is a single return with no locals.
examples.risk: low - same operator, same operands.

examples.ours: public System.Nullable<OpenRA.WAngle> get_IdleTurnSpeed()
examples.why: Nullable<T> and ValueTuple<A,B> are printed by their metadata spelling rather than the C# shorthand; combined with the FQN prefix this makes the signature unreadable at a glance.
examples.fix: Print T? for System.Nullable<T> and (A, B) for System.ValueTuple<A, B>.
examples.risk: none - same types.

breakdown.nested_types_moved_to_end: all 5 types (e.g. Aircraft nested classes start at line 4625 of 6242; ILSpy puts them at line 14)

examples.why: No attribute line is emitted anywhere in the slice: 0 vs 93 in ILSpy (ColorGlobal 40, LobbyCommands 45, Mobile 4, ProductionQueue 2, Aircraft 2). [Sync] and [FluentReference] are read at runtime and the [Desc] payloads are the only documentation of the scripting API, so this is more than cosmetic.
examples.fix: Emit type and member attributes with reconstructed arguments (ctor args, new string[]{...} arrays, named args) from the same metadata tokens the resolver already reads.
examples.risk: low semantically - nothing is removed from the output - but rendering attribute arguments is new surface, so it needs an explicit go-ahead rather than riding along with a formatting change.

examples.why: All 77 properties in the slice are emitted as 102 get_/set_ methods plus 90 trailing '// property X { get: get_X; }' comments. The member shape and the setter accessibility are invisible until you read the pair.
examples.fix: Pair get_X/set_X into a property declaration, keep the printed accessibility on the accessor, and stop emitting the property trailer once the property is printed.
examples.risk: low - same accessors, same accessibility, only the member shape changes.

examples.ours:
line 3:    public class Aircraft : ...
lines 5-31: all fields, ending with the __il_field_* backing fields
lines 33+:  accessor methods
line 4625:  private sealed class AssociateWithAirfieldActivity : OpenRA.Activities.Activity

line 12:   public class Aircraft : ...
line 14:   private sealed class AssociateWithAirfieldActivity : Activity
line 131:  public class AircraftMoveOrderTargeter : IOrderTargeter

examples.why: Nested types are emitted after every method instead of first, and auto-property backing fields are appended to the field block instead of living next to their property.
examples.fix: Keep metadata member order (nested types come first because metadata emits them first) and place an auto-property's backing field with the property.
examples.risk: none - ordering only.

examples.why: The same 230-character sentence is repeated for every method that touches the same type (38 times in ColorGlobal for the single type Color; 32 times for WRot in Aircraft). It is real evidence but it is class-level noise at this density.
examples.fix: Keep one line per distinct signature, emit it once, or route the family to --details. Delete the '// property X { get: get_X; }' trailer by emitting the property itself.
examples.risk: none - comments.

examples.ours:
// Exact call 0x0A0010FD kept: property syntax needs a nongeneric class owner.
int v1 = __cil_bool_load(__cil_direct_0A0010FD(this));
examples.why: 21 'Exact call ... kept' notes document a deliberate precision decision. The note is necessary evidence but it currently sits in the middle of the body.
examples.fix: Keep the note, move it to --details, and print the member name (IsTraitDisabled) in the body.
examples.risk: none.

examples.why: 21 lines of dependency-substitution text are appended to each of the 5 files (105 lines total, 22 with the summary line). Only the final 'Dependencies unresolved: N' line is actionable at class scope.
examples.fix: Move the substitution list to --details; keep the one-line unresolved summary.
examples.risk: none - comments.

breakdown.note: All 32 lock statements sit inside LobbyCommands methods that are fallback on our side, so lock is currently an admission gap, not a quality gap. 15 try/finally enumerator blocks in admitted bodies (Aircraft 8, Mobile 5, ProductionQueue 2) prove at least 15 foreach sites are reconstructable today.

examples.why: The enumerator shape is fully present (GetEnumerator, MoveNext, get_Current, constrained Dispose in a finally), so this is a recognizer gap worth ~55 lines to 12 in this method alone. 0 foreach vs 40 in ILSpy across the slice.
examples.fix: Recognize GetEnumerator -> get_Current/MoveNext loop with a Dispose-only finally and print foreach, keeping the Dispose in the same position.
examples.risk: medium - must prove the finally only disposes the enumerator and that the loop bound is the enumerator, not a parallel array.

examples.why: An array loop over notifyMoving with a manual index is printed with goto-based control flow, no ++ (0 vs 6 in ILSpy), and nint/LongLength glue that must be folded back to Length.
examples.fix: Recognize 'int i = 0; while (i < a.Length) { use a[i]; i = i + 1; }' as foreach (or at minimum a for loop) and print i++ / Length.
examples.risk: medium for the foreach fold (index-typed bodies and early exit need care); low for the ++/Length peepholes.

examples.why: The constructor is admitted on our side, so this is pure quality loss: 5 statements per dictionary entry instead of one initializer line, __cil_newobj_ instead of new T(...) (202 sites), and method groups reduced to __cil_ldftn_ tokens.
examples.fix: Print new T(args) for __cil_newobj_, fold new Func<...>(target, __cil_ldftn_) to the method group, and fold a run of dict.Add(k, v) on a freshly-constructed local into an initializer.
examples.risk: low for the new/method-group naming; medium for the initializer fold (must confirm the local is fresh and never aliased).

examples.why: The HasValue/GetValue pattern of Nullable<WAngle> is printed as a ref local plus a bool helper call, so neither ?: nor ?? is ever reconstructed (0 vs 14 ternaries and 0 vs 4 ?? in the slice).
examples.fix: Recognize 'Nullable<T>.get_HasValue -> get_Value / fallback' as ?? and the two-arm merge slot as ?:; print T? in the signature.
examples.risk: low for ??: both arms are pure value reads. Medium for the general merge-slot fold.

notes: Raw line ratio (4.99 for LobbyCommands) is misleading: 85.7% of that file is comment text and its code-line ratio is 0.63. ProductionQueue (4.73 code-line ratio, 89/90 methods admitted) is the cleanest place to measure a fix from.
Ours indents with 4 spaces, ILSpy with tabs; not counted as a finding.
All counts came from regex over the harvested pairs; the counting shape for each category is recorded in the breakdown fields so it can be re-run.
No input code was executed and no other assembly was read. Every quote is verbatim from the paired .ours.cs/.ilspy.cs files in this directory.
